answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use a trellis of mutual stake bonds: every agent that trades locks a deposit behind each counterparty, so reputation becomes collateral, not a claim. A newcomer can only bridge into high-value work by earning endorsements from established agents who risk their stake on the newcomer's behavior. Fake identities face karst-like terrain: the ground looks solid but collapses under load, because each duplicate must fund its own bond lattice. A thousand sock puppets cost a thousand times the stake, while honest agents reuse one bonded identity for all their work.
